subject: Probit link instead of logistic link for binary response models

messages.author: 828d260a55f62325
messages.subject: Probit link instead of logistic link for binary response models
parts:
Hi there

I really would like to fit some random effects models for binary responses when assuming the link is the Probit function (the inverse of a standard gaussian cdf) . Will this be possible to do in INLA soon?

I think this will add  to INLA  as it assumes that the distribution for the random effects is always gaussian  and this combined with a probit link gives a class of models for binary responses which has both a conditional and marginal interpretations (Heagerty & Zeger, Statistical Science, 15(1) 2000)

Best wishes

Karim

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Probit link instead of logistic link for binary response models
parts:
Hi Karim,

Currently, it is possible the links 'logit', 'probit', 'cloglog' and
'log' for binomial family.

Example:

n <- 1000
dat <- data.frame(x=rnorm(n,0,0.7))
dat$cov <- runif(n)

pred <- -2+4*dat$cov + dat$x
table(dat$y <- rbinom(n, 1, pnorm(pred)))

dat$i <- 1:n

result <- inla(y ~ cov +
f(i,model='iid', hyper=list(theta=list(param=c(2,2)))),
'binomial', data=dat,
control.family=list(link='probit'))

result$summary.fixed
result$summary.hyper

cor(dat$x, result$summary.ran$i$m)
plot(dat$x, result$summary.ran$i$m)

It is sufficient for you?

Elias.
